thread:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel routing tweak last night we're seeing more frequent OOMs on some 80GB hosts for long-chat workloads. Symptoms: high KV cache fragmentation + big prefetch windows that blow workspace budgets.

marta: Yep saw a spike in OOM rate around 01:12UTC. kv.frag_ratio jumped from ~0.22 -> 0.68 on a few nodes, and decode tail latency increased. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

ryan: I ran a quick flamegraph on one of the repros. Main hot paths are small churny allocations in the slab allocator during prefetch. Lots of demote+reclaim cycles.

ryan: Profiler snippet:```
alloc_slab(size=64) x 12k
free_slab(size=64) x 11.6k
alloc_slab(size=128) x 7k
coalesce_ops x 120
kv_prefill_bytes=1.9GB
workspace_peak=25.4GB (host has 32GB free before run)
```

sara: Interesting — seems like prefetch windows are too aggressive for these sequence lengths. We should consider lowering default prefetch cap and enabling a per-request "slimcap" that limits how much KV we pre-allocate per request.

alex: I sketched an idea: adaptive ejector + slimcap. Goals: 1) bound per-request prefill to a fraction of workspace (configurable), 2) when fragmentation > threshold, run an ejector that demotes oldest high-offset KV slots first and attempt slab coalesce lazily, 3) route oversized requests to slower kernel variant (lower memory footprint) instead of failing.

marta: +1. Also add a cheap heuristic: if concurrent_infers > N and frag_ratio > 0.5 then reduce prefetch window by 40%. That buys headroom without full disable.

ryan: Proposed metric additions to dashboards: [kv.prefetch_bytes], [kv.prefetch_per_request], [kv.frag_ratio], [allocator.fragmented_bytes], [allocator.coalesce_ops], [decode.throttle_cycles]. Need these for canary.

alex: Repro steps I used:```
# reproduce local-ish
python tools/run_load.py --model redwood-3b --seq 2048 --concurrency 12 --prefetch 1.0 --trace kv --duration 5m
# check logs: tail /var/log/redwood/serve.log | grep OOM
```

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary deployment queued to pool gpu-080 (3 hosts) with tag "ejector-slimcap-v1".

marta: Quick config diff I want to try (pseudoyaml):```
kv_prefetch:
  strategy: adaptive
  per_request_slimcap_frac: 0.12  # <= 12% of host workspace
  frag_threshold: 0.45
  frag_backoff_pct: 0.4
  prefer_demote: true
allocator:
  coalesce_on_free: lazy
  slab_sizes: [64,128,256,512,1024]
  max_small_slab_excess: 64MB
```

ryan: One extra kernel-level fallback we discussed: when total workspace free < X, switch model route to kernel variant K2 that uses chunked-attention with lower KV memory (costs ~1.2x CPU but avoids OOM). Should be a quick route policy change.

alex: Risk notes: 1) too-low slimcap increases decode latency (lost cache locality) 2) overly eager coalesce may spike CPU 3) demote logic must preserve correctness for in-flight streams.

sara: For correctness we need to ensure demote is only for ephemeral prefetch slots, not pinned tokens in active request. Maybe mark prefetch slots with TTL and skip pinned ones.

marta: Experiment plan:
- Phase A (lab): run 6 variants with per_request_slimcap in [0.06,0.12,0.2], frag_backoff_pct [0.3,0.5], coalesce_on_free lazy vs eager. Capture allocator.* + kv.* metrics.
- Phase B (canary): deploy best lab config to 3 hosts (infra-bot queued). Watch kv.frag_ratio, OOM count, tail latency for 24h.
- Rollback to previous config on any >2x OOMs or >15% tail latency regression.

ryan: I ran quick lab A run with slimcap=0.12 and lazy coalesce. Results: kv.frag_ratio reduced ~15%, OOMs dropped to 0 in 30m run, small 3% tail latency bump. Good signal.

alex: Nice. Let's add a synthetic perf test that stresses demote path specifically (long sequential prefixes + random prefetch). I'll add to ci-perf.

sara: Who wants to own canary monitoring? I can set up alerts for kv.frag_ratio > 0.5 and allocator.coalesce_ops rate > 200/min.

marta: assigning myself to tune runtime flags for the canary and document the rollback steps. alex you own perf regression guardrails and monitoring dashboards.

alex: Sounds good. I'll post a short troubleshooting playbook in the thread after I update dashboards.

ryan: small note — we should also consider a lightweight allocation sampler to sample per-request KV prefill sizes (don't sample all requests). That will make the metrics cheaper.

alex: +1. Action items: add metrics, deploy canary, run 24h, collect results, then decide rollout.

marta: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-status: canary started on gpu-080 hosts at 02:08UTC. Will report health every 10m.

alex: thanks — keeping thread updated with early numbers. If anyone sees an OOM tag me directly.
